newsitem.title: USA: Tensor Corp. recalls halogen bulbs that shattered.
newsitem.headline: Tensor Corp. recalls halogen bulbs that shattered.

text.p: Tensor Corp. of Chelsea, Mass., is recalling about 100,000 500-watt halogen bulbs sold in floor lamps after many shattered and started fires, the Consumer Product Safety Commission said Monday.
The tubular bulbs, which were made in China, were sold in 50,000 torchiere-style Tensor floor lamps, the commission said in a statement.

It said the Massachusetts company was aware of 281 incidents in which the bulbs had shattered, causing at least six burn injuries and some small fires. Three of the fires resulted in more than $25,000 in damage, it said.

"The bulbs may shatter during use, presenting a fire hazard when hot fragments of the shattered bulb land on nearby combustible materials, such as furniture, bedding, newspaper or carpet," the statement said.
The lamps with the affected bulbs were sold nationwide from October 1995 through April 1996 by Montgomery Ward and Electric Ave. & More stores, the statement said.
It said the model number "LT609N" or "LT609P" and a manufacturing plant code appear on stickers on the bottom of the lamp base.
